extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and evaluating petitions to revive abandoned patent applications under 37 CFR 1.137, including what constitutes an "unintentional" delay, required statements/evidence, timing thresholds, terminal disclaimer requirements, and special rules for provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire delay must be unintentional
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by a statement that the entire delay in providing the required reply from the due date for the reply until the filing of a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Office is almost always satisfied by applicant/representative statements (and sometimes copies of relevant correspondence), the Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional (see 37 CFR 1.137(b)(4)). Failure to carry the burden to establish that the 'entire' delay was 'unintentional' may lead to denial of the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended delay (> two years) requires additional explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition to revive an abandoned application is filed more than two years after the date the application became abandoned, the Office requires additional information beyond the statement of unintentional delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The additional information should establish facts and circumstances surrounding the entire delay to support a conclusion that the entire delay was unintentional. Electronic ePetition options exist but substantive additional facts are required for >2 year delays. See Clarification of the Practice for Requiring Additional Information in Petitions ... (85 FR 12222-24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate course of action is not an unintentional delay (enumerated examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: A delay resulting from a deliberately chosen course of action by the applicant cannot be considered 'unintentional' under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of deliberate choices that render delay intentional include: (A) applicant does not consider the claims patentable over outstanding references; (B) applicant does not consider allowed/patentable claims broad enough to justify expense; (C) applicant does not consider any patent sufficiently valuable to justify expense of obtaining a patent; (D) applicant does not consider any patent sufficiently valuable to maintain interest in obtaining it; (E) applicant remains interested but seeks to defer patent fees and prosecution expenses. A later change of mind does not render the earlier deliberate decision unintentional (see In re Maldague).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three delay periods considered when evaluating petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Three periods are considered during the evaluation of a petition under 37 CFR 1.137: (A) the delay in reply that originally resulted in the abandonment; (B) the delay in filing an initial petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application; and (C) the delay in filing a grantable petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137 to revive the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each period may be examined for intent; deliberate choice at any of these stages can render the overall delay intentional and preclude revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness safe-harbors: file within 3 months of first notice and within 1 year of abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office does not generally question whether delay was intentional when a petition is filed (A) within 3 months of the date the applicant is first notified that the application is abandoned; and (B) within 1 year of the date of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are advised to file within 3 months of first notification to avoid questions of intentional delay. If not filed within 3 months, the Office may require further information showing how the delay was unintentional. If not filed within 1 year, the Office may require information about when the applicant first became aware of the abandonment and how the delay in discovering the abandoned status occurred. To avoid procedural delay, include those showings when filing late.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof to establish unintentional delay when questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a question whether the entire delay was unintentional, the Office may require the applicant to carry the burden of proof to establish that the delay was unintentional within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. and 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though a mere statement is usually sufficient, when questions arise applicants should provide supporting facts/correspondence. See Application of G for precedent. Failure to meet the burden can result in denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party whose delay is relevant — identify who had right/authority to reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant question under 37 CFR 1.137 is whether the delay by the party having the right or authority to reply (or not reply) to avoid abandonment was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant assigned entire right, title, and interest to a third party (so applicant has no legal/equitable interest), the applicant's delay is irrelevant and the third party's actions govern. Where a third party controls prosecution, its decision is binding on the applicant unless the contract expressly makes the third party act solely in a fiduciary capacity. Agreements giving control without fiduciary limitation bind the applicant to the third party's prosecution choices (see Kim v. Quigg, Winkler, Futures Technology Ltd. v. Quigg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer must accompany petition in specified circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(d) requires that a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in specified application types and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required for: (A) design applications; (B) nonprovisional utility applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995; (C) nonprovisional plant applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995. Also required for certain utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000 if abandoned during appeal, interference, or secrecy order (because of eligibility for patent term extension). Terminal disclaimer must dedicate a terminal part of the term to the public equivalent to the applicable period. Filing a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for showing unintentional delay, nor does an unintentional delay waive the disclaimer requirement. Applicants may petition under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee) for waiver only in extraordinary situations where justice requires it (e.g., abandonment caused no actual delay). See MPEP § 1490.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration and timing for renewed petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137(e) requires any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application to be filed within 2 months of the decision (or within such time set in the decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless the decision indicates otherwise, this 2-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136. If a renewed petition, request for reconsideration, or other petition seeking review is filed outside the time specified, the Office may require a specific showing as to how the entire delay was unintentional. Deliberate choices not to persist in seeking revival remain immaterial to later explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application revival — limited to establishing pendency up to 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 is applicable to provisional applications abandoned for failure to reply to an Office requirement, but a provisional application will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) for a provisional must be accompanied by any outstanding reply. 35 U.S.C. 111(b)(5) treats a provisional as abandoned 12 months after filing and not subject to revival after such 12-month period. It is permissible to file a petition later than 12 months only to revive the application as pending for the 12-month period following filing (i.e., revive pendency up to the 12-month cutoff). Note extensions to next business day if 12-month date falls on weekend/holiday per 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Access to the file of an abandoned published application (non-IFW) may be available via the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch upon payment of fees; access to an abandoned unpublished application may be provided upon written request when the abandoned application is identified or relied upon in certain documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access permitted when the abandoned application is identified in a U.S. patent application publication or patent, statutory invention registration, or an international application published per PCT Article 21(2). Identification requires application/serial number and filing date, first named inventor, title and filing date, or similar application-specific information. A copy of application-as-filed or specific documents may be provided upon written request and payment per 37 CFR 1.19(b); Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv). See MPEP § 103 for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of abandonment — calculation rules and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is considered abandoned after midnight of the date on which the set shortened statutory period (including any extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) plus 1 month) expired; this is normally the day after the expiration of the shortened statutory period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how weekends and federal holidays affect the date of abandonment and the extension of the reply period per 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7. Examiners should verify actual abandonment and check Board files for allowed claims to avoid erroneous treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's statement on petition to set aside examiner's holding (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.181 permits the Director to direct the examiner to furnish a written statement, within a specific time, setting forth reasons for the examiner's decision on matters averred in the petition, with a copy to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless requested, such a statement should not be prepared. See MPEP § 1002.01 for additional direction.
